content_of_post_to_comment: We worry about AI sycophancy as if humans hadn’t been telling each other what they want to hear for centuries. About AI hallucinations as if our own minds didn’t routinely distort, confabulate, and misremember. About AI reinforcing our biases as if we hadn’t always gravitated toward people, ideas, and information that confirm what we already believe. AI might be the first technology that makes us systematically suspicious of cognitive behaviours we’ve always considered perfectly human.
comment: Maybe AI's real disruption is that it makes our biases visible at scale. Human self-deception was easier to excuse when it stayed private; automation turns familiar flaws into systems we have to confront.
